title: Feelings and opinions
description: Say how you feel, what you like and what you think, and agree or disagree politely.

guide.title: Feelings happen to you
guide.text:
In Kannada you do not 'be' happy or tired; the feeling happens or comes to you. The person is in the dative, the feeling is a noun, and the verb is a form of aagu ('happen') or baa ('come').

ಖುಷಿ (khushi) happiness, ಸಂತೋಷ (santosha) joy: nanage khushi aaytu, 'I became happy, I am glad'.
ಬೇಜಾರು (bejaaru) boredom, low spirits, being upset: nanage bejaaraagide.
ಸುಸ್ತು (sustu) tiredness: nanage sustaagide, 'I am tired'.
ಭಯ (bhaya) fear: nanage bhaya aagtide, 'I am scared'.
ಕೋಪ (kopa) anger: nanage kopa bandide, 'anger has come to me' = 'I am angry'.
ನಿದ್ದೆ (nidde) sleep: nanage nidde bartide, 'I am sleepy'.
ಆಶ್ಚರ್ಯ (aashcharya) surprise: nanage aashcharya aaytu, 'I was surprised'.

The tense tells the story: aaytu (it happened - a reaction to news), aagide (it has happened - the state now), aagtide (it is happening - building up right now).

examples.english: I am very happy (to hear or see that).

guide.title: Likes and dislikes
guide.text:
ಇಷ್ಟ (ishta) is 'liking': nanage ee haadu ishta, 'I like this song'. tumbaa ishta is 'like very much'.

For a reaction to something you have just tried, use ishta aaytu, 'liking happened' = 'I liked it', and ishta aagalilla, 'I didn't like it'.

Praise: chennaagide (it is good/nice); tumbaa chennaagide (very nice); sooper! - the English word, used constantly.

Sympathy and dismay: ಪಾಪ (paapa) 'poor thing!'; ಅಯ್ಯೋ (ayyo) 'oh no!'; ಛೆ (chhe) 'tut, what a shame'.

guide.title: Giving an opinion
guide.text:
'I think that ...' is built with ಅಂತ (anta), which closes off the thought like a spoken quotation mark, followed by nanage annisutte, 'it seems to me': idu sari anta nanage annisutte, 'this is right - so it seems to me' = 'I think this is right'. Negative: annisalla; nanage haage annisalla, 'I don't think so'.

The thought comes first and 'I think' comes last - the reverse of English.

Other ways to give a view: ನನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾರ (nanna prakaara) 'according to me, in my view'; ಇರಬಹುದು (irabahudu) 'maybe, could be'.

Agreeing: ಸರಿ (sari) right; neevu heliddu sari, 'what you said is right' (heliddu = 'that which was said'); haudu, nija, 'yes, true'.

Disagreeing politely: haage alla, 'it is not like that'; nanage haage annisalla. To ask: nimma abhipraaya enu? 'what is your opinion?' or simply nimage enu annisutte? 'what do you think?'

phrases.english: I am very happy about that.
phrases.note: A reaction to good news. More formal: santosha aaytu.
bejaaru covers bored, fed up, sad and upset.
The o of kopa is long.
anta marks the end of the thought. Written: endu (ಎಂದು) ... annisuttade (ಅನ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ).
A warm response to good news or to a thank-you.
